newsitem.title: ITALY: Magistrates talk to Credito official over Olivetti.
newsitem.headline: Magistrates talk to Credito official over Olivetti.

text.p: Magistrates investigating the account's of troubled information and technology group Olivetti, talked to the director general of bank Credito Italiano on Sunday, Ansa news agency reported.
Ansa said magistrates in the northern town of Ivrea, questioned Alessandro Profumo for five hours over Olivetti's first half results.

Magistrates opened the probe earlier this month after Renzo Francesconi resigned as Olivetti director general and questioned the company's 1996 results, raising doubts about the true level of debt at the loss-making group.
Francesconi's comments led to panic selling of Olivetti shares on the Milan bourse and undermined the position of the firm's chief executive, Francesco Caio, who quit the company's board last week.
Credito's Profumo told Ansa after Sunday's meeting with magistrates that he was a life-long of Caio.
"But does it seem possible to you that an employee of a bank like me could have talked with a private company about its results?" he asked. He made no other comment.
Magistrates talked to Caio's brother, Maurizio, for four and a half hours on Saturday as part of their inquiries.
